newsitem.title: USA: UAW sees variation in Big Three auto pacts.
newsitem.headline: UAW sees variation in Big Three auto pacts.

text.p: United Auto Workers Vice President Ernest Lofton said Wednesday he believes there is an opportunity to tailor the union's tentative labor agreement with Ford Motor Co to meet the individual needs of General Motors Corp and Chrysler Corp.

"President (Stephen) Yokich has said that while we have pattern bargaining, we also understand that things have to be shaped to accommodate and meet the needs of the respective companies," Lofton told reporters at a meeting of the union's National Ford Council.

Lofton said he expects the council to overwhelmingly adopt the agreement with Ford, which requires the automaker to maintain jobs for at least 95 percent of its approximately 105,000 UAW hourly workers.

In the past, the union has negotatied a pattern-style agreement that applies the same terms and conditions to all three companies. Analysts have said the job guarantees Ford agreed to would be difficult for GM to match.
"We succeeded in what we set out to accomplish," Lofton said. "Job security is number one."
The tentative agreement, reached Monday, was approved Tuesday by the UAW executive board.
